justifications.type_expressiveness: Good use of enums for Expr, Value, BinOp, UnaryOp, and EvalError variants, though TypeError still carries a String message rather than a structured variant distinguishing operator/operand kinds.
justifications.error_handling: Typed EvalError with the three required variants and ParseError with offset; no panics in library code, but TypeError uses a String payload and a few unreachable!() arms exist (justified by exhaustive matching but undocumented).
justifications.api_ergonomics: Public types have sensible derives and Display impls, but there are no doc comments on any public items and ParseError/EvalError expose public fields/variants without documentation.
justifications.idiomaticity: Generally idiomatic with ?, matches!, recursive descent, and a borrowed linked-list Env, though byte-indexed tokenizer loops and some .cloned() on tokens are slightly less polished than typical idiomatic Rust.
